clue.text: Tiny contribution I'd placed in bowl over by clock

indicators.note: the letters of I'd are put inside the word for bowl over

parts.note: to bowl someone over is to wow them
taken as written, without the apostrophe
to clock someone is to hit them, to smite

explanation.surface: A tiny offering is dropped into a collection bowl that sits beside a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The widow's mite is the Gospel story of a poor widow giving two small coins, worth more than the rich men's gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical widow's mite is proverbial for a small gift given by someone with little to spare.

clue.text: Landing place with fifty percent changing hands

indicators.note: the left hand letter L is swapped for the right hand letter R

parts.note: fifty percent is a half

explanation.surface: A dock where half the cargo is traded between owners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' are left and right, abbreviated L and R: changing hands turns the L of HALF into R, giving HARF, after W.
explanation.definitionFit: A wharf is a quay where boats tie up, so it is a place for landing goods and passengers.

clue.text: Bones initially needed in experiment to do with teaching

parts.note: Bones is slang for a doctor (sawbones; also Dr McCoy in Star Trek), so DOC

indicators.note: the N goes inside the word for experiment

parts.note: an experiment is a trial

indicators.note: the first letter only of the word needed is used

parts.note: first letter of needed

explanation.surface: A lesson where bones are required for a classroom experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctrine is what is taught, so doctrinal describes matters of teaching or belief.

clue.text: Chap set a switch incorrectly; pay attention in future!

indicators.note: the letters of these words are set out wrongly, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man has wired a switch wrongly, and someone warns that trouble will follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase tells listeners to keep watching for later developments, a call to stay alert to what comes.

clue.text: The implication is one would let in old Scottish lord

definitions.text: The implication is one would let in
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read cryptically as the answer: a duff (useless) mac (raincoat) is one that would let the rain in
first meaning: the Thane of Fife in Shakespeare's Macbeth

explanation.surface: A hint that someone would admit an aged Scottish nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Duff is British slang for faulty, and a mac is a raincoat, so a defective one lets water through.
explanation.definitionFit: Macduff is the Thane of Fife in Shakespeare's Macbeth, a Scottish nobleman of old.

clue.text: Vicious female gets sir wound up

indicators.note: wound up as in twisted or agitated, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spiteful woman annoys a knight until he is furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigress is the female of the big cat, and figuratively a fierce, aggressive woman.

clue.text: Arena, somewhere you go round in reverse

indicators.note: the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: a lav, the lavatory, is where you go to relieve yourself
a round shape, a ring, is the letter O

explanation.surface: A sports ground where you run laps the opposite way.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, which makes it a natural example of an arena.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval is an elliptical sports ground, as in the Kennington stadium, so it serves as an arena.

clue.text: Servant present finally after so long in Rome

indicators.note: the final letter comes after the Latin word

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

indicators.note: the last letter of the word present is used

parts.note: last letter of present

explanation.surface: A servant hands over a present at last after a long wait in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a manservant who looks after a gentleman's clothes and personal needs.

clue.text: Dream location maybe, where you only get green lights?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sleep, where dreams happen

definitions.text: where you only get green lights?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a land where everyone nods, giving approval or the go-ahead

explanation.walkthrough: A nod is a sign of approval, the green light, so a whole land of nods gives nothing but permission.
explanation.definitionFit: The Land of Nod is a jocular term for sleep, where dreams take place.

clue.text: Bug I planted on advocate to be avenged

parts.note: to bug someone is to get to them, annoy them
I is the numeral one
seeds planted are sown
to advocate a cause is to back it

explanation.surface: A spy hides a listening device on a lawyer in order to take revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to take revenge, to pay someone back for a wrong done.

clue.text: Stern and bow of ship going in one sudden movement

indicators.note: the S is put inside the combined letters

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a ship, so its first letter

parts.note: first letter of ship
a tic is a sudden involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: The back and front of a vessel lurch together in one jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks nautical beside 'bow of ship', but it is the adjective, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic person is severe and self-denying, so stern in their austerity.

clue.text: Cause of malfunction of foreign government changing leader

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: the Kremlin stands for the Russian government

explanation.surface: An overseas regime breaks down when it replaces its head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary mischievous creature blamed for unexplained mechanical faults.

clue.text: One who's retiring to keep hotel by remote country dwelling

parts.note: remote means far away

indicators.note: the H is held within the word for a shy person

parts.note: a retiring, timid person is a mouse
H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A retiree keeps a hotel beside a distant rural home.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmhouse is the main residence on a farm, a typical rural home.

clue.text: Closing bars best at Henley, perhaps, when whiskey's run out

indicators.note: the W is gone, taken away from the word

parts.note: to outrow a rival is to beat them in a rowing race, as at Henley Regatta
W is Whiskey in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Drinkers at the Henley regatta celebrate a win until the whiskey is finished and the bars shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' looks like pubs closing, but these are bars of music. Henley is a Thames town famous for its rowing regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: An outro is the concluding passage of a song, the last few bars of music.

clue.text: One swallowed an orange juice after returning hot

indicators.note: the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone gulps down an orange juice after coming back from the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Jonah was swallowed by a great fish, so he is the famous swallowed man.

clue.text: Heaving bag into the sea after approval from Hans?

indicators.note: the sea-and-bag piece comes after the German yes

parts.note: ja is German for yes, and Hans is a typical German name

indicators.note: the word for bag goes inside the sea

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
a pack is a bag carried on the back

explanation.surface: A German approves before someone throws a bag overboard into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A heaving place is crammed with people, which is what jam-packed means.

clue.text: One might get bite in water tank, following one earlier

definitions.text: One might get bite in water

indicators.note: these two letters come before the word for tank

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
I is the Roman numeral for one
the Sherman was an American tank of the Second World War

explanation.surface: Something in a water tank might bite, after an earlier one did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water tank' reads as one object, but 'in water' belongs to the definition and 'tank' alone is the Sherman.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler hopes for a bite from a fish while their line is in the water.

clue.text: Ruin a jam after smashing a pot

indicators.note: after being smashed to bits, the letters of these words are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spoils a jar of jam after breaking a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like the thing smashed, but it is the definition, slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is a slang name for cannabis, which is the drug also called marijuana.

clue.text: Drink from tap's to sell

parts.note: tap is (tap's) means milks, as in exploiting a resource
to tout goods is to try to sell them

explanation.surface: A drink comes from a tap that someone wants to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk stout is a sweet dark beer brewed with lactose, so a type of drink.

clue.text: Does away with secure feature of delivery

parts.note: to off someone is slang for killing them, so offs
to secure is to pin in place

explanation.surface: Someone dispenses with a fastening on a package being delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler's delivery is the ball bowled, and off spin is one way of turning it.
explanation.definitionFit: Off spin is a style of cricket bowling, a characteristic of how the ball is bowled.

clue.text: Pathologist's outside, I see, after sample of enzyme

indicators.note: the pathologist and see pieces follow the word for sample

parts.note: to sample something is to try it
the outside letters of pathologist, P and T
I see written as letters, I and C, since C sounds like see

explanation.surface: A pathologist stands outside after taking a sample to test for an enzyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Tryptic describes trypsin, the digestive protein catalyst, or processes caused by it.

clue.text: I'm surprised to find a Communist being driven with Poles

parts.note: O is an exclamation of surprise
a Red is a Communist

explanation.surface: Astonishment at discovering a Communist being chauffeured with Polish companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland, but they are the long oars, lowercase in meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that is oared is propelled with oars, long wooden shafts like poles.

clue.text: Misbehave in a court — in a court!

parts.note: to be up before a judge is to be in court

explanation.surface: Someone behaves badly in a courtroom, and the repetition stresses the outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase does two jobs; the second time it means being up before the magistrate, the British idiom for appearing in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to behave badly or play up, as an unruly child does.

clue.text: Current minister to set about Republican

indicators.note: set about here means placed around, so the word for minister to wraps the R

parts.note: to minister to someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: A present-day clergyman prepares to tackle a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a clergyman, but 'minister to' is a verb meaning care for.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is the current direction or fashion, the way things are flowing.

clue.text: Sail in front of dishonest judge, interrupting what he's telling?

indicators.note: the dishonest judge pieces break into the middle of the other word

parts.note: a dishonest judge would be telling a fib
lying means dishonest

explanation.surface: A boat sails past a crooked judge who keeps breaking into the story he is spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying jib is a triangular headsail set ahead of the jib at the very front of a ship.

clue.text: Rest? One may be needed during it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pause or rest

definitions.text: One may be needed during it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in snooker a rest (the cue support) may be needed during a ..., a scoring visit to the table

explanation.walkthrough: The 'One' refers back to 'Rest', in its snooker sense of a stick that supports the cue for long shots.
explanation.definitionFit: A break is a pause from work, and in snooker a run of scoring shots by one player.

clue.text: Joint protection from men on board, with movement for peace

parts.note: chessmen: K for king and N for knight

indicators.note: a movement of the letters of peace means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Chess pieces team up with a peace campaign to protect a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement for peace' reads as a campaign like CND, but the movement is applied to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A kneecap is the bone that covers and shields the front of the knee joint.

clue.text: Bun to have when consuming most of a pop

indicators.note: the word for to have swallows up the other piece

parts.note: to take something is to have it

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a pop means each, as in a pound a pop

explanation.surface: A bun to enjoy alongside a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like a soft drink, but 'a pop' means apiece, giving EACH; most of it is EAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a sweet yeasted bun, usually toasted and buttered.

clue.text: Queen alter The Colour of Money for radio

indicators.note: on the radio words are heard rather than seen, so this signals a sound-alike

parts.note: to alter the colour of something is to dye it, and dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: A queen changes the title of the film The Colour of Money for a radio version.
explanation.walkthrough: The Colour of Money is a Paul Newman film, a red herring: 'alter the colour' is DYE, 'of' links, 'money' is DOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido was the legendary queen of Carthage, abandoned by Aeneas in Virgil's epic.

clue.text: Trinket taken from jug — gift we might pick up

indicators.note: picking up means hearing, so the words are matched by sound

parts.note: jug and nick are both slang for prison; said aloud nick is the same as the first half of the answer
a gift for something is a knack

explanation.surface: A small ornament lifted out of a jug is a present someone might collect.
explanation.definitionFit: A knick-knack is a small decorative ornament of little value, like a bauble.
